app._comment: Static PWA (index.html at repo root, no build step, no root package.json). Served with `python -m http.server 8080` from the repo root; gate.py never starts this itself (checked: nothing in gate.py reads app.start), so the operator running the gate must have that server already up at app.url before running the e2e/a11y_ux domains, or those two will fail closed with connection errors rather than reporting real findings. This local server does NOT apply the repo's `_headers` file (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) -- those only apply on Cloudflare Pages -- so header-dependent checks here understate what production actually sends. Routes are hash-based SPA routes read from route() in index.html, not guessed: '/' defaults to today's or the latest post; /#/map, /#/ladder, /#/kodex, /#/discover are fixed views; /#/doc/{slug} fetches corpus/{slug}.md (only ai-pr-review and mcp-sensitive-data exist on disk today); /#/2026-07-25 pins a specific day's post and will need updating as the daily post rotates -- it is largely redundant with '/' (same view type) and can be dropped or re-pinned in a later edit without weakening coverage, since '/' already exercises the daily-post view.

unit._waiver_history: WAIVED 2026-07-27 on a WRONG diagnosis, LIFTED 2026-07-29. The waiver claimed the daemon was not running. It was: pid 9784 had held :8788 since 2026-07-22, answering /health 200 and a bare GET 401. The real fault was POST /chat returning 500 from a week-old process whose Claude Agent SDK runtime had gone stale. Restarting it fixed the domain: 10 pass, 0 fail. Two lessons kept here rather than in a commit message. First, 'connection refused' was assumed and never measured; `curl -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:8788/health` would have cost nothing. Second, the daemon wrote its stderr nowhere, so the 500 had no trace; it now appends to state/_daemon.log, which is how the restart was confirmed.
unit._comment: Runs the whole tests/ directory as of 2026-07-29; it was pinned to tests/boundaries.test.ts back when that was the only file, which meant a new test file would sit in the repo and never gate anything. Measured 2026-07-29: 22 pass, 0 fail, 35 expect() calls across 2 files. tests/mentor.test.ts is pure logic, hermetic, ~60ms: it lifts the המנטור queue block out of index.html and evaluates it, because the app is one inline script with no module boundary and a hand-copied fixture would drift. It carries a regression oracle for the suppression bug found the same day (a belief is keyed semantically, so suppression must match belief.from, not the belief id; proven to fail against the previous logic before the fix). tests/boundaries.test.ts is NOT hermetic and the gate must not be read as if it were: it makes an authenticated, state-mutating (self-restoring) round trip against the LIVE production Cloudflare Worker at https://sadna-sync.shovalb9.workers.dev, and 4 of its 10 tests require a local daemon answering on http://localhost:8788 (started separately via `cd daemon && bun run server.ts`). If that daemon is not running when the gate executes, those 4 fail closed with connection-refused rather than being skipped. COVERAGE BOUNDARY: this domain is example-based and integration only. There is no property-based, mutation, fuzz or contract testing anywhere in this repo, and the gate has no domain for any of them; filed 2026-07-29 to claude-setup as a gap against work-docs/testing_practices.txt section 6.

waived.reason:
REWRITTEN 2026-08-08 because the previous waiver went STALE, correctly, and its own root-cause attribution turned out to be wrong. Both facts are kept here rather than quietly replaced.

WHAT THE STALE FIRING PROVED. The old confirm string was '#themeToggle', pinned on the claim that flow.py falsely calls that working toggle dead. An accessibility pass added aria-pressed, an action-oriented aria-label and a toast to it and to #sndToggle, which pushed both over flow.py's 24-character body-innerHTML gate. Both vanished from the dead-control list, the confirm string stopped appearing, and the gate failed the domain. That is the waiver-confirm feature working exactly as designed: the claim stopped being true and the waiver refused to outlive it.

MEASURED MOVEMENT, same command, same 8 routes, mobile: 40 fail to 28 fail. Flow findings 17 to 4. Tap targets 20 to 21. Contrast 3 to 3.

THE FLOW DOMAIN IS NOW HONEST AND CAN BE READ. All 4 remaining dead controls were individually driven over CDP with flow.py's own click_js and are understood, not assumed: the #flat2d tree tab and #tab-kodex are CORRECTLY idempotent (pressed while already active, renderPanel rebuilds byte-identical, delta 0 and nodes 424 to 424 across 3 trials each), and neither sets aria-current or aria-pressed, so the no-op is invisible to a screen reader, which is a real accessibility gap and not a flow one. The /#/ladder details summary could NOT be reproduced as dead: 5 isolated trials in both directions move innerText by 1251 characters, two orders of magnitude over the threshold, yet flow.py reports it dead in every full 8-route run. Unexplained; the working hypothesis is a boot race under the concurrent CDP load a full run generates, and it is unconfirmed. The discover anchor is a positional selector over rotating content: three runs resolved it to three different real GitHub links, so 'is this control dead' is not answerable by that selector at all.

THE ATTRIBUTION THIS WAIVER INHERITED WAS WRONG, and this is the part worth carrying forward. Every previous version said the tap-target failures were 'roughly 15 talent-board node labels at about 70x23' and that they were blocked because DESIGN.md freezes the board geometry. Measured now: /#/map, which IS the talent board, has ZERO tap-target failures. 19 of the 21 are on /#/ladder and 2 are on /#/2026-07-25. They are research-ladder row links rendering at heights like 198x17 and 226x17. The board-geometry freeze that blocked this work for two weeks DOES NOT APPLY to them. This is now ordinary line-height work on a surface nobody has rejected five design passes for.

CONTRAST DID NOT MOVE. Still 3, and the same values: 2.92:1 and 1.35:1 on /#/map and 1.05:1 on /#/ladder. The a11y pass added theme-invariant --board-* tokens for exactly this and the numbers are unchanged, so those tokens are not reaching the failing labels. That is an open, unexplained gap, not a fix awaiting confirmation.

The confirm string is now the 1.05:1 finding on /#/ladder, because that is the single most specific thing this waiver asserts is still broken. When it is fixed the waiver goes stale, which is correct.

That is an accurate report of the app's current state, not a contract defect.

waived.reason:
Reads state/e2e/last.json and expires with the e2e waiver. Rewritten 2026-08-08 against a fresh report: 28 fail, 371 warn, down from 40 and 373. Of the 28, 24 belong to this domain: 21 tap targets and 3 contrast.

The important correction is where they are. 19 of the 21 tap targets are on /#/ladder and 2 on /#/2026-07-25. The talent board at /#/map has none. Every earlier version of this waiver blamed board node labels and invoked the DESIGN.md geometry freeze as the reason the work was blocked. That reason does not survive measurement, and the work is not blocked by it.

The 3 contrast failures did not move at all: 2.92:1 and 1.35:1 on the board and 1.05:1 on the ladder, byte-identical to the pre-fix run. A pass that added --board-ink, --board-ink-dim, --board-faded and --board-gold-hi as deliberately theme-invariant literals, and darkened light theme's --gold from #8a6d34 to #775e2d, moved none of them. Either the failing labels do not use those tokens or the audit grades a state the tokens do not cover. Nobody has established which, and this waiver does not pretend otherwise.

What that same pass DID fix is real and is on the record next to the miss: the .part-head .ask control measured 1.56:1 because it is a real button with no declared background while :root sets color-scheme: dark, so Chrome painted the UA form-control face, an opaque rgb(107,107,107), behind muted text. Confirmed live over CDP rather than inferred. It no longer appears in the report.

Genuinely reduced on 2026-08-08, not renewed unchanged. CI now runs 38 of the 48 tests in tests/ (5 of 6 files: mentor.test.ts, decks.test.ts, contract.test.ts, fuzz.test.ts, mutation.test.ts), added as a new step in .github/workflows/ci.yml. All five read index.html and daemon/server_parse.ts directly (server_parse.ts has zero imports of its own) and open no network connection, so they run on any runner with no secret; verified locally at the pinned bun version (1.3.14) before this commit, 38 pass, 0 fail. That is a real coverage increase, not the whole unit domain: tests/boundaries.test.ts (10 tests) stays local-only, excluded on purpose rather than deleted from the suite. Its top-level await on the gitignored daemon/.key means the whole file fails to import without that file present, so no -t filter can rescue a subset in CI. Its 5 worker: tests need a real SYNC_KEY secret this repo does not have (`gh secret list` returns only CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), and its 5 daemon: tests need a daemon process with its own Claude Agent SDK credential that no GitHub runner here starts. Adding either secret is a production-adjacent decision this waiver does not make for itself. The Chrome clause in the prior reason is retracted, not renewed, because it is now measured wrong: GitHub's own ubuntu-latest image ships Google Chrome 150.0.7871.128 with a CDP-capable driver (confirmed from actions/runner-images' Ubuntu2404 README), so 'needs a Chrome CDP endpoint' is no longer the blocker for e2e. The real remaining blocker for e2e, for the review domain, and for the gate's own primary path (gate.py run) is one fact, not three: flow.py, panel.py and gate.py all live in ShovalBenjer/claude-setup, confirmed private ('private':true via gh api). Running any of them here means either a new PAT secret scoped to a private admin repo used inside a PUBLIC repo's CI job, or vendoring those three files into daily-deep-learning, which is out of this task's edit scope and a separate content decision (claude-setup internals landing in a public repo). Neither happened here; both are real, named decisions, not a quick fix. Honesty note for the next reader: ci_runs_gate's fallback match checks only the LAST TOKEN of each contract cmd against the workflow text. unit's cmd ends in 'tests/', and the new CI step's command contains that substring, so the builtin will read unit as matched once this waiver lapses. It is covered for 5 of 6 files; tests/boundaries.test.ts is not, and this note exists so that substring match is never mistaken for full unit coverage. New expiry set to 2026-08-15 to align with the e2e and a11y_ux waivers in this same file, since all three now turn on the same claude-setup access decision, not because the date slipped.

Correction to the paragraph above, not a replacement: private repo access is not the only blocker for e2e, it is the first of two. Even with claude-setup readable from Actions, claude-setup/tools/browser/cdp.py's chrome_path() (lines 79 to 90) hardcodes three Windows-only paths and calls SystemExit if none exist, and launch() (lines 245 to 278) only reaches that Windows-only fallback after failing to adopt an already-listening debug port. So a GitHub runner having Chrome preinstalled does not help flow.py start it: a CI step would still need to launch Chrome itself with the remote-debugging flag first, which is unwritten work on top of the access decision, not a consequence of solving it. Also worth naming for the next reader: a new hermetic test file added to tests/ has to be added to the ci.yml step by name, the same way this contract's own unit domain once sat pinned to a single file and gated nothing new until it was widened; the CI step does not glob tests/, so it will not pick one up on its own.

pipeline._cmd_comment: This cmd exists only to produce the waived.confirm string above. The pipeline domain is still evaluated by builtin ci_runs_gate whenever it is NOT waived, and eval_domain checks builtin before cmd (gate.py:939 runs before :950), so this cmd never drives the real verdict while the waiver is live. It must be deleted, not left in place, in the same commit that lifts or removes the waiver: ci_runs_gate builds its own fallback token list from every domain that has a cmd (cmds = [d.get("cmd") for d in domains.values() if d.get("cmd")]), so once this domain is no longer short-circuited by waived, its own confirm-only cmd would be added to that list too, and the trailing whitespace-split token of this cmd (a literal quote character after the word CI) does not appear in any workflow file, which would fail the domain on its own confirm plumbing instead of on a real gap. Verified 2026-08-08: computed the trailing token of every OTHER domain's cmd in this contract and grepped it against the concatenated text of ci.yml, deploy.yml and claude-code-review.yml. build (tools/validate_links.py), unit (tests/), types (tools/gen_art.sh) and review (the literal ".") all match something in a workflow file. e2e (state/e2e/last.json) is the only one that does not, which is the exact and only real gap this waiver is about.
